issues.title: Fix ETS usage in for linksafe
issues.body: Previously, we'd try to delete from ETS using a full entry instead of just its key. Fix the usage of :ets.insert_new and :ets.delete

issues.title: rudimentary acquire_linksafe, release_linksafe.
issues.body:
- rudimentary safe versions of acquire and release, such that the calling process' semaphore acquisitions get cleaned up upon an exit (unclean or otherwise).
- named `acquire_linksafe`, etc to be consistent with the existing precedent `call_linksafe`.
- also fixes a bug that caused concurrent "call-safe" acquisitions to be broken - calls to `call_linksafe` et al no longer leak.
    - why: ets only considers one tuple element as the key for any entry. so for us, using the ets defaults, only the first tuple element (sempahore name) was considered the key. in a set, all writes with the same semaphore name resolve to the same key regardless of other tuple elements, so `insert_new` does not actually insert items into the call-safe table if another for the same semaphore already existed.

issues.title: Revise `call_linksafe/3` to keep track of multiple procs per semaphore
issues.body:
Before, `call_linksafe/3` used an ETS set to store a single PID per semaphore key, which does not allow for appropriate sweeping when a semaphore is acquired by more than one process at once.

The linksafe table has been changed to an ETS bag (multiple unique PIDs per semaphore key), along with appropriate related changes. The function test has also been extended to ensure correct behavior in the normal case, as well as when multiple dead procs require sweeping.

issues.title: Add Semaphore.Resource, for creating module semaphore's
issues.body:
Better as a seperate library?

Can be used to limit access to expensive resources.

issues.title: decrease-max-fix
issues.body:
Fixes the behaviour of the `acquire/2` function when you provide a `max` which is less than the current count.

See the issue for more details: https://github.com/discord/semaphore/issues/6
